subject: Cloud Computing
title: Google and Microsoft Enter the Race
description: One-minute skill: Google and Microsoft Enter the Race.

hook.text: By 2008, Amazon had a two-year head start. Google and Microsoft scrambled to catch up.

buildup.text: Google launched App Engine in 2008, targeting developers who wanted zero server management.

discovery.text: Microsoft launched Azure in 2010, betting that enterprises would trust a familiar name.

twist.text: Google had the best tech but couldn't sell to businesses. Microsoft had the relationships.

climax.text: Today AWS leads, Azure is second, Google Cloud third. Three companies dominate the market.

punchline.text: Three giants split the cloud. Everyone else fights for scraps.

quiz.question: Why did Microsoft Azure gain traction despite launching years after AWS?
options: Enterprises already trusted Microsoft from decades of business software
Azure was completely free for the first five years

details.summary: Google launched Google App Engine in 2008 and expanded into Google Cloud Platform. Microsoft launched Azure in 2010, leveraging its enterprise relationships. Both validated the cloud market and created the three-way competition that drives innovation and price reductions today.
details.whyItMatters: Competition between AWS, Azure, and GCP pushed cloud prices down and innovation up. The three-way race benefits every cloud customer through better services at lower cost.
takeaways: Google App Engine launched in 2008, Azure in 2010
Microsoft leveraged enterprise relationships for Azure adoption
Three-way competition drives innovation and lowers prices

faq.question: Why did Microsoft enter cloud computing?
faq.answer: Under CEO Steve Ballmer and accelerated by Satya Nadella, Microsoft recognized that cloud was replacing on-premises software. Azure let Microsoft maintain enterprise relationships while transitioning customers from Windows Server and SQL Server to cloud equivalents.

faq.question: What was Google's cloud advantage?
faq.answer: Google brought unmatched expertise in large-scale distributed systems, having built technologies like MapReduce, BigTable, and Borg internally. Google Cloud Platform offered these capabilities as services, attracting data-intensive and engineering-focused customers.
